steps.content: A long while after that, you finally find an opportunity to ask to take Ignis out.
It's been a long time since you left the Bureau.
There are no jobs, no crises, and not even any kitchen explosions. Just an ordinary walk down the street, a moment of peace.
Ignis is standing before you, without her usual attitude, looking just like an ordinary girl.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Did you say you were taking me to a cafe? Why are you... staring at me?
After a turn, you get to the planned cafe. You sit on the second floor near a window, where you can clearly see across the street.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: If you say anything, I'll trigger my ability.
You laugh and take her through the crowd, down a narrow alley to a little shop.
Finally, you get to the planned cafe. You sit on the second floor next to a window, where you can clearly see across the street.
There's a little store there that doesn't draw the eye, with no name on the door and no sign, but warmly decorated with flowers and candlesticks.
As soon as she sees it, Ignis's eyes are fixed on it. She looks confused and hesitant.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: No, it just seems nice. Is it a family flower shop?
No, a family restaurant.
Ignis's shoulders shudder next to you, as if she's surprised. She has figured it out.
This is the restaurant your parents started. It's open now... Do you think they're there?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: What are you trying to do?!

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I didn't agree to this... I didn't agree...

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: You liar!
She bangs the table and grabs you by the collar.
Hearing the commotion, a waiter appears. You wave a little and smile apologetically.
Calm down. Do you want to add to your arson file?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Why you... I'll—
The temperature drops. All she does is shake her fist and bite her lower lip.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I want to go back!
It's teatime, they have a lot of customers. If you go downstairs now you might be seen.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: You jerk... I'm really going to burn this...
Relax. No one here knows your family, and your parents won't be able to see who's sitting on the second floor. You could sit up here watching them all day without having to worry.
If you're unhappy, I can go.
You stand up as you speak, preparing to leave.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: ...Wait!

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Don't... Don't go downstairs. What if my ability... Don't go too far! But...

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: But! I don't want to look at your ugly face today!
You turn around, and pull up a chair behind her, sitting back-to-back.
She doesn't make a sound, which you take as consent.
The tense atmosphere slowly relaxes. In the low light, you see her hands pressed to the window, gazing across the street. Then you look too.

It's peaceful, and the place is filling up with customers. They all have satisfied smiles, and people are constantly calling into the store. It looks like they have good relationships with the owners.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I didn't know they were here... Why did you bring me here?
I know you don't want to bother them. But just watching doesn't count as bothering them.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: ...Okay.
Do you want to see your new family member?
It is silent behind you. It seems like Ignis is struggling to make up her mind.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I'm... Let's wait.
You lean on the window and look at the diners coming and going across the street. If your intel was good, her new family member should be inside.
It looks like she's still not ready.
Maybe eating something will change your mood? It's our lucky day, your family's restaurant has started doing takeout.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: No. I'm happy just looking.
Her ponytail brushes your shoulder. Her voice was quieter just now.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: No.
Then I'll get something.
Two crème brûlée.
You express your regret while calling out to the waiter by the stairs. He nods and leaves.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: You... Forget it. You have no idea what that dessert means.
What does it mean?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: We once made crème brûlée together. My mom and dad prepared it, and I was responsible for the last step, burning the sugar. Mom and dad hoped practice would teach me to control my ability.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: But of course I failed, and burned down the garage. That's when I gave up on cooking.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: But on that day, when trying to clean up the mess in the garage, we find a crème brûlée that survived.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: But there was one lucky thing. For a moment I got the fire under control, and succeeded, and it tasted really good.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Dad was also happy, and said it was the best crème brûlée ever. Beaming with pride, he said he wanted a new shop sign, and gave it a really embarrassing name.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: How did you know? No...

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Are you going through my blog's data again?
She wheels around, and doesn't talk to you anymore.
Fortunately, the waiter comes back with two desserts on the plate.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: The crème brûlée you ordered, bought from the shop across the way. Bon appetit.

They are crème brûlées like you can get anywhere, but on second glance you can see they are something special. The color is beautiful, the aroma is lovely, and the thin layer of sugar on top is perfectly caramelized.
You really don't want any?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: I said I don't. You eat it.
But there are a few small letters there...
And a little label with something written... Ignis...
She grabs the plate and turns her back toward you.
The air fills with quiet sobs.
You silently start eating the crème brûlée. There is a small, delicate label standing on the dessert, which says "Ignis' Kiss."
It really is delicious, and you can feel that a lot of emotion went into it.
Her parents never "moved on" from her. This food, gradually becoming a trend all over the city, is a message to their long-lost daughter.
You don't know if she's eating, or whether it tastes the same to her.
Are you alright?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Hmm...

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: They... should have forgotten me. They have... a new daughter.
The bonds of family are a gift from fate. You always thought that your existence was making them unhappy, but your existence also made them very fortunate. Isn't that the meaning of life?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: You're... so annoying... you shouldn't... shouldn't have...
She's complaining, but she's also letting out emotions she hasn't had a way to express for a long time. Now that the dam has started to break, they're pouring out without end.
You aren't family, you aren't her friend, and you aren't her savior. You're just her jailer. But here, in this moment, you've done what you could for her.
That day, you sit together until they close up shop and Nightingale sends you a reminder. She uses her private communicator to get in touch, and tells you that it's time.
Ignis's parents never come outside, and Ignis is a little disappointed, but she seems more relieved. Maybe she still wasn't ready.
All you remember is that she grabs the corner of your shirt, lowers her head, and eventually asks a question.

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Can we... come back here?

steps.speaker: Ignis
steps.content: Just here is okay, here is fine. I don't want to be a bother...
You don't answer her, just nod silently.
Of course, no matter how many times. Until she is finally brave enough to push open the door and go home.
